# Sources: ICP and personas for outbound

Read 2026-10-29. "Read" means the
primary text was in hand. "Summary only" means only an abstract, a catalog record or a third-party summary was
reached, and nothing from it is quoted as the author's words.

## Persona origin (design lineage)

- Cooper, A. (2008), "The origin of personas", Cooper Journal, 15 May 2008. Recovered from the Internet Archive
  (live URL dead): https://web.archive.org/web/2013id_/http://www.cooper.com/journal/2008/05/the_origin_of_personas.html .
  Read. The 1983 persona was a play-acted user based on one interviewee ("Kathy"); the 1995 personas (Chuck,
  Cynthia, Rob) were split by goals, tasks and skill levels, and formalised to persuade clients.
- Cooper, A. (1999), The Inmates Are Running the Asylum, Sams. Table of contents only: chapter 9 holds a section
  titled "It's a User Persona, Not a Buyer Persona" (p. 135). Section body not read.
- Goodwin, K. (2001, 2002), two Cooper Journal articles on persona method, archived. Read in the September
  research. "Personas represent behavior patterns, not job descriptions"; "provisional personas" when there is
  no research; "every aspect ... tied back to real data".
- Pruitt, J. and Grudin, J. (2003), "Personas: Practice and Theory", DUX 2003, DOI 10.1145/997078.997089.
  https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/pruitt-grudinold.pdf . Read. Microsoft's
  method: 3 to 6 personas from segmentation data, a foundation document with footnotes, an anti-persona, a
  feature-by-persona matrix; "We have not tried to formally measure the impact of our Personas".
- Grudin, J. and Pruitt, J. (2002), "Personas, Participatory Design and Product Development", PDC 2002. Read
  (September). Source of the "Patrick" persona with 21 attributes.

## Persona evidence and critique

- Chapman, C. N. and Milham, R. P. (2006), "The Personas' New Clothes", HFES 50th Annual Meeting, pp. 634-636.
  https://cnchapman.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2007/03/chapman-milham-personas-hfes2006-0139-0330.pdf .
  Read. Personas cannot be falsified, so they cannot be validated.
- Chapman, C. N., Love, E., Milham, R. P., ElRif, P. and Alford, J. L. (2008), "Quantitative Evaluation of
  Personas as Information", HFES 52nd, pp. 1107-1111.
  https://quantuxbook.com/papers/REPRINT-HFES08-chapman-love-milham-elrif-alford.pdf . Read. Six real datasets:
  descriptions with 9 or more attributes match nobody at the 99th percentile in 5 of 6.
- Matthews, T., Judge, T. and Whittaker, S. (2012), "How do designers and user experience professionals actually
  perceive and use personas?", CHI '12, DOI 10.1145/2207676.2208573. Read in the September research: 11 of 14
  practitioners did not design with personas; they kept the role information and ignored personal detail.
- Friess, E. (2012), "Personas and decision making in the design process", CHI '12, DOI 10.1145/2207676.2208572.
  Abstract only. Advocates rarely invoked their personas while deciding.
- Nielsen, L. and Storgaard Hansen, K. (2014), "Personas is applicable", CHI '14. Read in September: personas
  provide a common language; more than 10 becomes hard to use.
- Salminen, J., Chhirang, K., Jung, S.-G. and Jansen, B. J. (2021), "Instilling Knowledge Claims of Personas
  from 346 Research Articles", CHI '21 EA, DOI 10.1145/3411763.3451619. Summary only. Most persona claims lack
  strong evidence, including "three to seven personas" and "about 47,000 US dollars per project".
- Salminen, J., Jung, S.-G., Nielsen, L. and Jansen, B. J. (2022), NordiCHI '22, number of personas. Abstract
  read. Demographic coverage kept improving up to 40 personas on 250 million video views.
- Kaate, I., Salminen, J., Jung, S.-G., Olkkonen, R. and Jansen, B. J. (2023), EMAC 52nd, paper 112368.
  https://proceedings.emac-online.org/pdfs/A2023-112368.pdf . Read (first pages). "the value of personas for
  marketing has not been systematically studied".
- Amin, D. et al. (2025), "Creating and Evaluating Personas Using Generative AI: A Scoping Review of 81
  Articles", arXiv 2504.04927. Abstract and v1 read. 45% of studies do not evaluate; risk of circularity when one
  model writes and judges.
- Salminen, J., Amin, D. and Jansen, B. J. (2025), "Using AI for User Representation: An Analysis of 83 Persona
  Prompts", arXiv 2508.13047. Abstract read. Model-made personas carry demographics almost always.

## Buyer personas (marketing lineage)

- Revella, A. (2016), The Buyer Persona Manifesto, 2nd ed., Buyer Persona Institute.
  https://www.buyerpersona.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/Buyer-Persona-Manifesto-2016.pdf . Read in full
  2026-10-29. Names and defines the 5 Rings of Buying Insight (priority initiatives, success factors, perceived
  barriers, buyer's journey, decision criteria); "six to ten interviews"; interview buyers who decided "in the
  past several months"; quote the buyer's own words; claims insight-based personas need "half as many".
- Revella, A. (2015), Buyer Personas, Wiley. Not read; the manifesto is her own short form of it.
- Zambito, T. (2002 onward), "buyer persona" coinage, tonyzambito.com. Read in September: research-based
  archetypes of "who buyers are, what they are trying to accomplish, what goals drive their behavior, how they
  think, how they buy". The link to Cooper rests on interviews, not on his own pages.
- ITSMA (2017), "Role-Based Profiles Are NOT Buyer Personas", 2 May 2017, and ITSMA 2018 ABM benchmark. Read in
  September. Second-hand profiles are "heavy on demographics and pain points, but light on insight into actual
  buying behavior"; rule of thumb of "three or fewer distinct personas".
- Cintell (2016), "Understanding B2B Buyers: The 2016 Benchmark Study", with Marketing Advisory Network.
  https://unleashpossibledotblogdotcom.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/final-benchmark-study-understanding-buyers-2016-cintell-2.pdf .
  Read in September. n=137 self-selected, self-reported; origin of "2x more likely to exceed goals".

## Jobs to be done

- Christensen, C. M., Hall, T., Dillon, K. and Duncan, D. S. (2016), "Know Your Customers' Jobs to Be Done",
  Harvard Business Review, September 2016; and Competing Against Luck (2016). Opening only (paywall).
- Moesta, B. and Engle, G. (2020), Demand-Side Sales 101, Lioncrest. Publisher and retailer listings checked
  (https://lioncrest.com/books/demand-side-sales-101-stop-selling-and-help-your-customers-make-progress). Book
  not read; method known through summaries.
- Jobs-to-be-Done.org, "The four forces". https://jobstobedone.org/the-four-forces/ . Read. "Bob Moesta and Chris
  Spiek developed the four-forces model"; push, pull, anxiety, habit, each defined.
- Klement, A. (2016), When Coffee and Kale Compete, and Intercom's job stories ("When ..., I want to ..., so I
  can ..."). Summaries only (e.g. https://mountaingoatsoftware.com/blog/job-stories-offer-a-viable-alternative-to-user-stories).
- Ulwick, A. / Strategyn, Outcome-Driven Innovation. Read in September; the "86% success rate" traces to 18 of 21
  client launches, self-rated.
- Romaniuk, J. (2022), Category Entry Points in a B2B World, LinkedIn B2B Institute with Ehrenberg-Bass. Read in
  September. Every buying situation has two perspectives: the business and the professional ("not getting
  fired").

## Canvases

- Gray, D. (2017), "Updated Empathy Map Canvas", XPLANE, and the canvas PDF (c) 2017 Dave Gray, updated 16 July
  2017 (copy: https://mchnutritionpartners.ucla.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Empathy-Map-Canvas.pdf). Medium
  post blocked (403); canvas and secondary descriptions read. Origin at XPLANE, popularised in Gamestorming
  (Gray, Brown, Macanufo, 2010). 2017 version adds a goal ("WHO are we empathizing with? What do they need to
  DO?") and puts think and feel inside the head.
- Osterwalder, A., Pigneur, Y., Bernarda, G. and Smith, A. (2014), Value Proposition Design, Wiley; Strategyzer
  page https://www.strategyzer.com/library/the-value-proposition-canvas . Page read; book not read. Customer
  profile = jobs, pains, gains; value map = products, pain relievers, gain creators; "Fit is a claim until
  customers confirm it."

## Awareness

- Schwartz, E. M. (1966), Breakthrough Advertising, Boston Book Club (reissued). Book not read. Every reachable
  web page gives the five levels in modern labels (unaware, problem aware, solution aware, product aware, most
  aware) without quoting the book; one author says he "compiled them" himself
  (https://bma.beehiiv.com/p/swiped-from-a-279-book). The idea (match the message to what the reader already
  knows) is Schwartz's; the exact modern labels are not verified as his.

## Buying groups and sales methods

- Wind, Y. and Cardozo, R. N. (1974), "Industrial Market Segmentation", Industrial Marketing Management 3(3).
  Paywalled, not read; the two stages (macro on the organisation, then micro on the people inside) are read from
  Choffray, J.-M. and Lilien, G. L. (1980), Market Planning for New Industrial Products, p. 332 (September
  research).

- Adamson, B., Dixon, M., Spenner, P. and Toman, N. (2015), The Challenger Customer, Portfolio; CEB deck "An
  Introduction to The Challenger Customer" (2015). Read in September (deck). Purchase likelihood by group size
  (n=3,000, not monotone); positioning value to one individual stakeholder -4%, collective learning +20%. Seven
  stakeholder profiles (Go-Getter, Teacher, Skeptic as mobilizers; Friend, Guide, Climber as talkers; Blocker):
  https://challengerinc.com/the-challenger-customer-profiles/ .
- Dixon, M. and Adamson, B. (2011), The Challenger Sale, Portfolio. Not read; teach, tailor, take control is its
  standard summary.
- Gartner (2025), press release 7 May 2025, survey of 632 B2B buyers. Read in September. Individual-level
  relevance: "59% negative impact" on consensus; group relevance: buyers "three times more likely" to report a
  high-quality deal.
- Webster, F. E. and Wind, Y. (1972), "A General Model for Understanding Organizational Buying Behavior",
  Journal of Marketing 36(2). Abstract only. The five buying-centre roles are a conceptual model.
- Winning by Design, SPICED (Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical Event, Decision). Company pages and summaries only
  (https://resources.rework.com/libraries/pipeline-management/spiced-framework).
- Ross, A. and Tyler, M. (2011), Predictable Revenue. Summaries only: a written ICP before prospecting; seeds,
  nets, spears.

## Outbound practitioners

- 30 Minutes to President's Club with Gong, "The Ultimate Cold Email Data Report" (85M+ cold emails).
  https://tactics.30mpc.com/hubfs/The%20Ultimate%20Cold%20Email%20Data%20Report-1.pdf . Read. "Executives don't
  care if you reference their alma mater"; reference business problems, not personal fun facts; pitch words
  lower replies; prospect-focused language. No method section beyond the email count.
- Gong, "How to master cold email ... 85 million emails".
  https://www.gong.io/resources/guides/how-to-master-cold-email-get-the-data-backed-guide-based-on-85-million-emails .
  Landing page only.
- Jason Bay (Outbound Squad, formerly Blissful Prospecting). Podcast pages and webinar transcripts only. His
  stated core of a cold email: say you solve a problem, ask if they have it.
- Josh Braun. Summaries of his "poke the bear" questions (e.g. https://www.11x.ai/guides/josh-braun-cold-outreach-method).
  Surface a problem the reader has not named; never a pitch first.
- Becc Holland (Flip the Script), via https://www.antoinebuteau.com/lessons-from-becc-holland/ . Personalisation
  (about the person) against relevance (about the role and context); when there is no personal premise, stay
  relevant to the role.

## Address (formal or informal)

- Leung, E., Lenoir, A.-S. I., Puntoni, S. and van Osselaer, S. M. J. (2023), "Consumer preference for formal
  address and informal address from warm brands and competent brands", Journal of Consumer Psychology 33(3),
  546-560, DOI 10.1002/jcpy.1322. Abstract and catalog only. Five studies: informal works better for warm brands,
  formal for competent ones.
- Kretzenbacher, H. L. and Hensel-Boerner, S. (2024), "Pronominal Address in German Sales Talk: Effects on the
  Perception of the Salesperson", Languages 9(10), 316. Summary only (MDPI 403). Du or Sie made no substantial
  difference overall; where it did, Sie was rated more positively. Cites Hensel-Boerner and Kords (2021): du gave
  no sales advantage.
- MDPI special issue "Perception and Processing of Address Terms" (2024).
  https://mdpi-res.com/bookfiles/book/12024/Perception_and_Processing_of_Address_Terms.pdf . Summary only.
  German and French participants rated recruiters higher with the formal pronoun.

## Classifying people from a profile

- Achananuparp, P. et al. (2025), FewSOC, arXiv 2511.12010. Summary only: default occupation labels in a resume
  dataset were about 63% accurate.
- "Digital Transformation and the Restructuring of Employment" (2025), arXiv 2506.23230. Summary only: a model
  sorting job titles into broad functions, about 92.6% accurate on 500 hand-checked titles.
- SOCbot (Sociological Methods and Research), DOI 10.1177/00491241261461516. Summary only: model coding of
  occupations close to trained human coders.
